questions.stem: This anterior view of the great vessels shows the aortic arch and its branches. Based on the branching pattern illustrated, how do the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries arise relative to the arch?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They share a common left brachiocephalic trunk

choices.label: B
choices.text: They both branch from a single brachiocephalic trunk with the carotids

choices.label: C
choices.text: They branch from the pulmonary trunk

choices.label: D
choices.text: They arise from the descending thoracic aorta

choices.label: E
choices.text: They arise separately and independently from the arch

explanation.summary: On the left, the common carotid and subclavian arteries arise separately and directly from the aortic arch, unlike the right side where a brachiocephalic trunk first divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. This asymmetry reflects the differing embryologic remodeling of the aortic arches.
explanation.whyCorrect: On the left, the common carotid and subclavian arteries arise separately and directly from the aortic arch, unlike the right side where a brachiocephalic trunk first divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. This asymmetry reflects the differing embryologic remodeling of the aortic arches.

questions.stem: This lateral view of an early embryo shows a series of ridges labeled as pharyngeal arches. The major arteries and connective/muscular structures derived from these arches ultimately supply which body region?

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lower back and vertebral column

explanation.summary: The pharyngeal (branchial) arches shown remodel to form the great arteries and other structures of the head, neck, and thorax. Somites, the heart bulge, lens placode, and otic placode are also visible, marking key landmarks of the developing embryo.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pharyngeal (branchial) arches shown remodel to form the great arteries and other structures of the head, neck, and thorax. Somites, the heart bulge, lens placode, and otic placode are also visible, marking key landmarks of the developing embryo.

questions.stem: This schematic traces the stepwise remodeling of the paired embryonic aortic arches into the adult great vessels. The distal segment of the left sixth arch that persists rather than regressing becomes which structure?

explanation.summary: The sixth aortic arches give rise to the pulmonary arteries; on the left, the distal segment persists as the ductus arteriosus, whereas on the right this distal portion regresses. This asymmetry also explains the differing courses of the right and left recurrent laryngeal nerves.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sixth aortic arches give rise to the pulmonary arteries; on the left, the distal segment persists as the ductus arteriosus, whereas on the right this distal portion regresses. This asymmetry also explains the differing courses of the right and left recurrent laryngeal nerves.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal aortic arch (left) with a congenital abnormality of the arch (right). In this defect, where is the narrowing most commonly located?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the bifurcation of the aorta into the common iliac arteries

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the aortic root within the sinuses of Valsalva

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the abdominal aorta at the level of the renal arteries

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the ascending aorta just above the aortic valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the descending aorta, just distal to the left subclavian artery

explanation.summary: Coarctation of the aorta is a stricture of the aortic lumen most often located in the descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery, near the attachment of the ligamentum arteriosum (the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus).
explanation.whyCorrect: Coarctation of the aorta is a stricture of the aortic lumen most often located in the descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery, near the attachment of the ligamentum arteriosum (the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus).

questions.stem: This clinical photograph shows bluish discoloration of the nailbeds, fingers, and toes in an infant. This physical sign is a direct marker of what?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elevated carboxyhemoglobin from carbon monoxide exposure

choices.label: B
choices.text: An elevated concentration of deoxygenated hemoglobin in the blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: An absolute deficiency of total hemoglobin (anemia)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased methemoglobin from an oxidizing drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess bilirubin deposition in the skin and mucous membranes

explanation.summary: Cyanosis is the bluish discoloration seen when the level of deoxygenated hemoglobin rises (roughly above 5 g/dL). In right-to-left shunting cyanotic CHDs, poorly oxygenated blood reaches the systemic circulation, producing peripheral and central cyanosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanosis is the bluish discoloration seen when the level of deoxygenated hemoglobin rises (roughly above 5 g/dL). In right-to-left shunting cyanotic CHDs, poorly oxygenated blood reaches the systemic circulation, producing peripheral and central cyanosis.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a young child assuming a squatting/knee-to-chest posture during a hypercyanotic 'tet' spell. Why does this position relieve the child's symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It raises systemic vascular resistance, which decreases right-to-left shunting across the VSD

choices.label: B
choices.text: It slows the heart rate, allowing longer diastolic filling of the left ventricle

choices.label: C
choices.text: It lowers systemic vascular resistance, increasing forward flow through the aorta

choices.label: D
choices.text: It increases pulmonary vascular resistance, forcing blood into the systemic circuit

choices.label: E
choices.text: It compresses the inferior vena cava, reducing venous return to the right heart

explanation.summary: Squatting kinks the femoral arteries and increases systemic (arterial) vascular resistance. This raises left-sided pressures, reducing the right-to-left shunt across the VSD so that more deoxygenated blood is directed through the pulmonary valve to be oxygenated, easing the tet spell.
explanation.whyCorrect: Squatting kinks the femoral arteries and increases systemic (arterial) vascular resistance. This raises left-sided pressures, reducing the right-to-left shunt across the VSD so that more deoxygenated blood is directed through the pulmonary valve to be oxygenated, easing the tet spell.

questions.stem: These schematics classify aortic coarctation by its position relative to the ductus arteriosus. The preductal type shown on the left is most likely the result of abnormal development of which embryonic structure?

explanation.summary: Congenital preductal coarctation is thought to arise from abnormal development of the aortic arch during formation from the embryonic left fourth aortic arch, whereas postductal lesions relate to abnormal development of the descending aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congenital preductal coarctation is thought to arise from abnormal development of the aortic arch during formation from the embryonic left fourth aortic arch, whereas postductal lesions relate to abnormal development of the descending aorta.

questions.stem: This diagram shows dilated collateral vessels (left subclavian, internal thoracic, and intercostal arteries) rerouting blood past an aortic coarctation. As these vessels enlarge, they classically produce which radiographic sign?

explanation.summary: The enlarged intercostal arteries erode the inferior surface of the ribs as they carry collateral flow to the lower body, producing the classic rib-notching sign on chest radiograph in coarctation of the aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: The enlarged intercostal arteries erode the inferior surface of the ribs as they carry collateral flow to the lower body, producing the classic rib-notching sign on chest radiograph in coarctation of the aorta.

questions.stem: This cross-sectional CT/MR angiographic image (arrow) provides a 3D picture used to plan intervention for which aortic abnormality?

explanation.summary: CT and MR imaging give a detailed 3D depiction of the narrowed segment and associated anatomic abnormalities of aortic coarctation, aiding planning of the appropriate intervention.
explanation.whyCorrect: CT and MR imaging give a detailed 3D depiction of the narrowed segment and associated anatomic abnormalities of aortic coarctation, aiding planning of the appropriate intervention.

questions.stem: These sequential catheter angiograms show a coarctation before treatment (left), during the procedure (middle), and after the procedure (right). Which intervention is depicted?

explanation.summary: Transcatheter intervention with placement of a percutaneous stent across the narrowed segment is the preferred approach in older children and adults with coarctation of the aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: Transcatheter intervention with placement of a percutaneous stent across the narrowed segment is the preferred approach in older children and adults with coarctation of the aorta.

questions.stem: The right-hand illustration contrasts a normal heart with an obstructive right-sided valvular lesion. Long-standing disease of this type leads to hypertrophy of which chamber?

explanation.summary: Pulmonary valve stenosis obstructs right ventricular outflow; the chronic pressure overload produces right ventricular hypertrophy and can ultimately lead to right heart failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pulmonary valve stenosis obstructs right ventricular outflow; the chronic pressure overload produces right ventricular hypertrophy and can ultimately lead to right heart failure.

questions.stem: The right-hand illustration contrasts a normal heart with an obstructive left-sided valvular lesion. This congenital lesion most commonly results from which valve morphology?

explanation.summary: Congenital aortic valve stenosis most often reflects a bicuspid aortic valve; having two cusps rather than three predisposes to fibrosis and calcification with worsening obstruction over time.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congenital aortic valve stenosis most often reflects a bicuspid aortic valve; having two cusps rather than three predisposes to fibrosis and calcification with worsening obstruction over time.

questions.stem: In this color-Doppler echocardiogram of a patent ductus arteriosus, what does the bright mosaic (multicolored) signal at the pulmonary-artery end most likely represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Normal antegrade flow across the pulmonary valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: A calcified thrombus occluding the duct

explanation.summary: The high pressure gradient from aorta to pulmonary artery accelerates flow through the duct; the resulting turbulence exceeds the Nyquist limit and appears as a mosaic of aliased colors on Doppler.
explanation.whyCorrect: The high pressure gradient from aorta to pulmonary artery accelerates flow through the duct; the resulting turbulence exceeds the Nyquist limit and appears as a mosaic of aliased colors on Doppler.

questions.stem: This photograph shows a patient with a PDA whose lower-extremity oxygen saturation (foot probe) is markedly lower than the upper-extremity saturation (hand probe). What mechanism best explains this pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A left-to-right shunt through an atrial septal defect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right-to-left shunting into the aorta distal to the head/arm vessels

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aortic coarctation located proximal to the left subclavian artery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Methemoglobinemia selectively affecting the lower limbs

explanation.summary: In Eisenmenger physiology the reversed PDA shunt delivers deoxygenated blood to the descending aorta beyond the arch vessels, so the legs appear cyanotic (differential cyanosis) while the upper body remains pink.
explanation.whyCorrect: In Eisenmenger physiology the reversed PDA shunt delivers deoxygenated blood to the descending aorta beyond the arch vessels, so the legs appear cyanotic (differential cyanosis) while the upper body remains pink.

questions.stem: This schematic depicts an atrial septal defect. Why does blood cross the defect in the direction shown rather than the reverse?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Left atrial pressure normally exceeds right atrial pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: The septal defect actively pumps blood toward the left

choices.label: C
choices.text: Right atrial pressure normally exceeds left atrial pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pulmonary artery pressure exceeds systemic arterial pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Gravity directs blood across the interatrial septum

explanation.summary: Because the left atrium operates at higher pressure than the right, an interatrial communication produces a left-to-right shunt, increasing pulmonary blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the left atrium operates at higher pressure than the right, an interatrial communication produces a left-to-right shunt, increasing pulmonary blood flow.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the normal sequence of fetal atrial septation. Failure of the septum primum to fuse with the endocardial cushions produces which type of defect?

explanation.summary: Persistence of the ostium primum from incomplete fusion of the septum primum with the endocardial cushions yields a primum ASD, located low in the atrial septum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Persistence of the ostium primum from incomplete fusion of the septum primum with the endocardial cushions yields a primum ASD, located low in the atrial septum.

questions.stem: This diagram illustrates formation of the interventricular septum. The membranous portion forms from fusion of the endocardial cushions, the aorticopulmonary septum, and which additional structure?

explanation.summary: The membranous IV septum completes when the muscular septum, the endocardial cushions, and the aorticopulmonary (conotruncal) septum meet; failure of this fusion is the most common cause of a VSD.
explanation.whyCorrect: The membranous IV septum completes when the muscular septum, the endocardial cushions, and the aorticopulmonary (conotruncal) septum meet; failure of this fusion is the most common cause of a VSD.

questions.stem: Comparing the normal heart with the heart with a VSD in this diagram, why is the oxygen saturation in the right ventricle higher than normal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coronary sinus blood draining into the right ventricle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Retrograde flow from aortic valve regurgitation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased oxygen extraction by the pulmonary circulation

explanation.summary: Oxygenated LV blood crosses the VSD into the RV, raising RV oxygen saturation (an oxygen 'step-up') detectable on catheterization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxygenated LV blood crosses the VSD into the RV, raising RV oxygen saturation (an oxygen 'step-up') detectable on catheterization.

questions.stem: This developmental sequence depicts formation of the interatrial septum. The flap-valve opening present in the final panel closes after birth and leaves which adult structure?

explanation.summary: The foramen ovale, bounded by septum primum and septum secundum, permits fetal right-to-left flow. When left atrial pressure rises after birth it seals, leaving the fossa ovalis as a depression in the adult atrial septum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The foramen ovale, bounded by septum primum and septum secundum, permits fetal right-to-left flow. When left atrial pressure rises after birth it seals, leaving the fossa ovalis as a depression in the adult atrial septum.

questions.stem: This cardiac image uses the colored overlay between the aorta and pulmonary artery to detect and grade a ductal shunt. Which imaging technique produces this colored signal?

explanation.summary: The mosaic color mapped onto the grayscale ultrasound is color Doppler, which encodes blood flow direction and velocity. It reveals the turbulent shunt jet of a patent ductus arteriosus between the descending aorta and pulmonary artery.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mosaic color mapped onto the grayscale ultrasound is color Doppler, which encodes blood flow direction and velocity. It reveals the turbulent shunt jet of a patent ductus arteriosus between the descending aorta and pulmonary artery.

questions.stem: This clinical photograph shows simultaneous pulse-oximetry readings from a foot and a hand in a patient with congenital heart disease. What phenomenon does the disparity demonstrate?

explanation.summary: A right-to-left shunt through a PDA delivers deoxygenated blood to the descending aorta distal to the head/arm vessels, so the lower extremities read a lower saturation than the upper extremities, producing differential cyanosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: A right-to-left shunt through a PDA delivers deoxygenated blood to the descending aorta distal to the head/arm vessels, so the lower extremities read a lower saturation than the upper extremities, producing differential cyanosis.

questions.stem: The highlighted abnormal vessel in this diagram is a persistent fetal connection that normally closes shortly after birth. Which factor is primarily responsible for its normal postnatal closure?

explanation.summary: The ductus arteriosus is kept patent in utero by low oxygen and high prostaglandin E1. After birth, lung expansion raises arterial oxygen tension, which triggers ductal smooth muscle constriction and functional closure within 15-30 hours.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ductus arteriosus is kept patent in utero by low oxygen and high prostaglandin E1. After birth, lung expansion raises arterial oxygen tension, which triggers ductal smooth muscle constriction and functional closure within 15-30 hours.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts two patterns of the second heart sound during inspiration and expiration. The lower pattern, which does not vary with respiration, is the classic auscultatory sign of which condition?

explanation.summary: Fixed, wide splitting of S2 (A2-P2 gap unchanged by respiration) reflects the equalized, respiration-independent right heart filling caused by the ASD shunt, a key physical-exam clue to atrial septal defect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fixed, wide splitting of S2 (A2-P2 gap unchanged by respiration) reflects the equalized, respiration-independent right heart filling caused by the ASD shunt, a key physical-exam clue to atrial septal defect.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram from a cyanotic neonate shows an aorta positioned above and straddling the interventricular septum, sitting over a septal defect. Which cyanotic congenital heart defect does this image represent?

explanation.summary: The echo demonstrates the overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect that are two of the four components of tetralogy of Fallot; the other two, pulmonary valve stenosis and RV hypertrophy, complete the tetrad.
explanation.whyCorrect: The echo demonstrates the overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect that are two of the four components of tetralogy of Fallot; the other two, pulmonary valve stenosis and RV hypertrophy, complete the tetrad.

questions.stem: This cardiac MR angiogram from an infant shows an enlarged right atrium, a markedly hypoplastic right ventricle, and no inlet from the RA to the RV. Which lesion does this represent?

explanation.summary: Absence of the tricuspid valve prevents RA-to-RV filling, so the RV receives little blood and becomes hypoplastic while the RA enlarges, the imaging hallmark of tricuspid atresia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absence of the tricuspid valve prevents RA-to-RV filling, so the RV receives little blood and becomes hypoplastic while the RA enlarges, the imaging hallmark of tricuspid atresia.

questions.stem: A neonate with a right-to-left shunt shows the bluish discoloration seen here in the nailbeds, fingers, and toes. This clinical sign results directly from an increased blood concentration of what?

explanation.summary: Cyanosis becomes visible when the absolute amount of reduced (deoxygenated) hemoglobin in the blood rises above roughly 5 g/dL, which occurs when a right-to-left shunt allows deoxygenated blood to bypass the lungs and enter the systemic circulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanosis becomes visible when the absolute amount of reduced (deoxygenated) hemoglobin in the blood rises above roughly 5 g/dL, which occurs when a right-to-left shunt allows deoxygenated blood to bypass the lungs and enter the systemic circulation.

questions.stem: This schematic shows a single arterial trunk arising from the heart that then divides into the aorta and pulmonary arteries. Failure of which embryologic process produces this defect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure of the truncoconal septum to divide the outflow tract

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the endocardial cushions to fuse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of the interventricular foramen to close

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of the sinus venosus to be incorporated

choices.label: E
choices.text: Failure of the septum primum and secundum to fuse

explanation.summary: Normally the truncoconal septum spirals down to separate the aorta from the pulmonary trunk; when this division fails, a single truncal vessel overrides both ventricles, defining persistent truncus arteriosus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normally the truncoconal septum spirals down to separate the aorta from the pulmonary trunk; when this division fails, a single truncal vessel overrides both ventricles, defining persistent truncus arteriosus.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram shows an aorta overriding a defect in the interventricular septum together with a thickened right ventricle. Which single diagnosis do these findings indicate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete transposition of the great arteries

explanation.summary: The study demonstrates an overriding aorta straddling a ventricular septal defect with right ventricular hypertrophy, the key anatomic features of tetralogy of Fallot; pulmonic/RVOT stenosis completes the tetrad.
explanation.whyCorrect: The study demonstrates an overriding aorta straddling a ventricular septal defect with right ventricular hypertrophy, the key anatomic features of tetralogy of Fallot; pulmonic/RVOT stenosis completes the tetrad.

questions.stem: This fingertip finding developed gradually in a patient with long-standing cyanotic congenital heart disease. What process is most directly responsible for it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Peripheral arterial occlusion causing digital ischemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune synovial inflammation of the interphalangeal joints

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acute bacterial infection of the nail bed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Chronic hypoxemia driving distal soft-tissue proliferation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Deposition of urate crystals in the distal joints

explanation.summary: The photograph shows digital clubbing, with loss of the normal nail-fold angle and bulbous fingertips. In cyanotic CHD such as tetralogy of Fallot, chronic hypoxemia promotes release of platelet-derived growth factor and VEGF, causing connective-tissue proliferation in the distal digits.
explanation.whyCorrect: The photograph shows digital clubbing, with loss of the normal nail-fold angle and bulbous fingertips. In cyanotic CHD such as tetralogy of Fallot, chronic hypoxemia promotes release of platelet-derived growth factor and VEGF, causing connective-tissue proliferation in the distal digits.
